name: Manlet / height tiers

lead: Manlet is forum slang for a man regarded as short, and height tiers are the informal brackets members use to rank men by height. The vocabulary frames why so many people in appearance communities work on height, lifts, posture and presentation.

There is no single mechanism; it is a way of classifying height and discussing how it shapes perceived status. Posters disagree about where the cutoffs sit. Medicine defines short stature as adult height more than two standard deviations below the mean for age and sex, roughly the shortest 2.3 percent of a population, which is separate from the community's brackets.

paras: People use the terms in advice threads, comparison photos and memes, then turn to practical options discussed alongside them such as lifts, posture, fit and clothing, and growth-focused routines for those still growing.

The term is used as a pejorative as well as a self-description. Medical sources describe teasing reported by short children, and one Swedish cohort study reported an inverse association between height and suicide risk in men, while noting most very short adults are not disabled by their height.

angle.text: Manlet and height tiers are the shorthand for how height is ranked in appearance communities, and they explain why users chase height gains, lifts and sharper presentation. It is a vocabulary rather than a method, and cutoffs vary by poster.

lead: Manlet is slang used on looksmaxxing forums such as looksmax.org for a man considered short, often used with the idea of height tiers: informal brackets of height used to rank men within the community. Posters disagree about where the thresholds sit, and threads exist both asserting and disputing particular cutoffs.

Medically, short stature is usually defined as adult height more than two standard deviations below the mean for age and sex, about the shortest 2.3 percent of a population, and common childhood causes include constitutional growth delay and familial short stature.[1] The community vocabulary is separate from this definition.

Height features heavily in forum discussion, where members post about perceived social disadvantage, rage threads, and 'heightmaxxing' options such as growth hormone secretagogues. The scientific literature on appearance and height cited here is limited.
infobox: Below 2 SD of mean for age and sex[1]

paras: Manlet is applied to men judged short, usually by the poster. Titles on looksmax.org use it for videos, fights, celebrity comparisons and personal threads, for example 'Manlet rage' and 'manlet problems'.[2][3] Height tiers refers to ranking by height bracket in the same culture, with the brackets decided by users rather than any authority.
The term is associated with the broader hierarchy vocabulary of the forum, including mogging, where a taller or more attractive person is said to outclass another.

In one thread, a teenage poster aged 17 who describes himself as 5'5 asks whether MK-677 would be worthwhile for height, citing side effects he has heard of such as grogginess, hunger, water retention and diabetes risk. Replies in the thread include advice to accept one's height and be confident, as well as rejection of that advice.[3]

Another thread describes the poster as short and expresses distress about being so, drawing a reply in the same terms.[2] Other threads present video clips of short men said to be outclassed, or mogged, by taller people.[4]

Short children often report being teased, though the encyclopedic summary notes that most very short adults are not physically or psychologically disabled by their height. A Swedish cohort study found a strong inverse association between height and suicide risk in men.[1]
The idea of a Napoleon complex, a purported link between short men and aggression, is described as a popular notion rather than an established condition.[1]

Growth hormone therapy for children with growth failure typically adds about 5 to 10 cm to predicted final height over years of injections, and critics have argued drug makers promoted short stature as a disease.[1]
No studies found on the community term or the height tiers themselves. Related research on short stature and growth hormone therapy in children is summarised in encyclopedic sources.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, manlet threads mix humour, self-deprecation and questions about height-increasing methods.[2][3]

claims.claim: Being short is a major, hard-to-change disadvantage (the 'heightpill').
Drugs like MK-677 can add height for a teenager who is short.
